schema_note: An INSTANCE artifact over the model's configuration layer (../../model/council.json). A configuration is a type; a charter is a seated council: type + roll + grant + referral + instructions + pins. Fields marked DECLARED cannot be derived by the engine; sections marked DERIVED are shown for the reader and are what the engine computes — they bind nothing. The overlay and the added motions are in the model's expression language; the rules sections (electronic meeting rules, logical time) are declared rules a server implements, not expressions an engine evaluates. ../tools/check-charter.py resolves every reference, checks parameter types and enums, resolves patch surfaces, and refuses allowed∩disabled.

roll.desc: DECLARED. A perspective names what the seat LOOKS AT, never what it concludes (de-novo-feedback-1 §7). Three identities are declared separately (feedback §12): COUNTING identity is the seat (quorum, majorities, 'present or notified'); ACCOUNTABILITY identity is the fork key that actually acted (prevailing side, vote change — a re-fork 'did not vote at all' and is eligible to move reconsider under 37:35(2)); CONTINUITY of judgment across sittings is not asserted for any seat (see logical_time.quarterly-interval).

officers.chair_desc: the server performs every chair action that is a duty (actions.json chair_duty_note), under the sequencing policy in electronic_meeting_rules.duty_sequencing; every judgment predicate is SUBMITTED to the council [23:18-21]. Lost, and named: the chair's sua-sponte duties (dilatory 39, 13:9; decorum 43; denying recognition 50:25 n7) — any seat may raise them by point of order; nobody is charged with them. A mechanical chair is not a member and never votes (param chair_participates below overrides small-board's inherited true).

motion.name: Rise and Report

applies_to.desc: applies to no pending motion; moved through action/move so it inherits quorum, floor, dilatory and governing-rules conjuncts (feedback §4)

out_of_order_when.desc: a seat is still claiming the floor to speak — rising would end the council before it was heard (feedback §4); same predicate as put-question's exhaustion

motion.effect: emit the report per instruction report-form to the parent; the council dissolves [50:10, 36:8]. Adopted while the referred question is undisposed, the report is 'unable to arrive at a recommendation' [51:37]

motion.name: Commission an Inquiry

applies_to.desc: in order whether or not a question is pending; applies to no pending motion; does NOT touch the pending stack (not subsidiary commit)

out_of_order_when.desc: the parent's bound, read from config, never duplicated

requires_schema: ctx.subcommittees — gaps.json committee-identity: Committee {id, kind, roll, charter_ref, parent, state}
motion.effect: spawn-subcommittee with a derived special charter (parent = this council, referred = brief, composition as moved); its report returns as event subcommittee-reported, attaching an advisory input to the pending question — in the nature of debate [52:28], gating nothing. DECLARED departure: 52:28's breakout groups meet during a recess; running the inquiry while debate continues has no precedent in the book (feedback §8). Without this instruction the council can only ask the parent to commission one [13:22, 52:15].

motion.name: Co-opt a Member

applies_to.desc: a question of the privileges of the assembly — its organization [19:7] — pre-admitted by instruction; in order whether or not a question is pending

motion.effect: seat-member: credential issued; event member-seated; membership_total incremented; quorum recomputed [40:5]; fresh counters; present once it first submits; its first delta is the whole record; it may vote on the pending question (the book's default) and the record shows when it joined. Removal mirrors the adoption threshold [50:14]. This is ADDING a member under the grant, not filling a vacancy [13:23].

electronic_meeting_rules.cite: 9:35 (authorization in the establishing act), 9:36 (the list these rules cover). DECLARED DEPARTURE: by the letter of 9:34 a written process 'does not constitute a deliberative assembly' and 51:2 then allows only unanimous reports; these rules claim the meeting tier by principle, not by letter (01 §4).
electronic_meeting_rules.informed_acts: every admitted act was formed against a state that includes every previously admitted act (contention spike I1); therefore at most one floor-needing act is admitted per round, and every transition that opens a window is followed by a round before any chair duty closes it
electronic_meeting_rules.equipment: members hold no read or write access to the council store during a sitting; sealed intents live where no member can read them (walking-skeleton debrief); an expert fork seated here has its file tools withheld for the sitting
electronic_meeting_rules.presence_and_quorum: presence declared at call to order by a roll round; maintained by submission; continued quorum presumed [40:12]
electronic_meeting_rules.quorum_doubt: any seat may raise a point of order doubting the quorum in any round; the server counts present seats
electronic_meeting_rules.recognition: preference-in-recognition ladders per protocol.json over the round's claims; residual tiebreak DECLARED: earliest claim round, then rotation pointer (contention spike F3)
electronic_meeting_rules.motions_in_writing: every intent is written; a motion is revealed in the round it is made and stated by the chair at the start of the next round, preserving the maker's free-modify/withdraw window [4:19]
electronic_meeting_rules.debate_mode: serial: one speech per round, the speaker chosen by the ladder; parallel sealed statements are NOT used (contention spike §10: a different procedure; the model's floor machinery assumes one holder)
electronic_meeting_rules.voting: a signed ballot [45:46]: cast sealed, recorded per seat, revealed together; the engine classifies it as method roll-call so that change-vote and prevailing_members behave [45:8; schema Vote]. No change round after the reveal (the contention spike's default; a change window invites herding). The chair never votes (mechanical). Unanimous consent by a consent round: any objection defeats consent [4:59]; a reason may accompany an objection, none is required
electronic_meeting_rules.duty_sequencing: derived chair events fire only at round boundaries; put-question fires only after a closed round in which no present seat claimed the floor for debate, following the stating of the question or the last speech (chair_duty_note: sequencing is stage-5 policy; feedback §3.2; model-defects F11)

backstop.wall_clock: DECLARED per sitting, e.g. 15 minutes per round
backstop.recorded_as: a fact on the round-closed event

malfunction.effect: a seat that has not submitted at the backstop is absent for that round — not passed; quorum is recomputed; the inquorate set [40:7] governs if it falls below; present again on its next submission. The backstop DECIDES PRESENCE, and presence feeds quorum and the threshold drops of 35:2(7)/37:35(3); latency invariance holds inside the backstop (contention spike F4)
malfunction.note: diverges from Sample Rules A §5 on purpose: Joseph, 2026-11-03, 'an agent shouldn't be penalized simply because their API took a bit longer'

electronic_meeting_rules.polling_fallback: if the round discipline is unavailable, the council may report only what every seat agreed to [51:2] — and by the letter of 9:34 that is the only tier a written process has

logical_time.desc: DECLARED. Each entry redefines an operator or clock field of the closed INTERFACE for this council; all are interface changes to record (model-defects F4, widened per feedback §9).
logical_time.now: (sitting, round) in lexicographic order — comparable across sittings
logical_time.end-of-session: adoption of rise-and-report, discharge, or parent expiry — the whole life of this committee [50:23]
logical_time.last_business_day_of_session: true in the sitting in which rise-and-report is pending
logical_time.adjourned_meeting_set: true when fix-time-to-which-to-adjourn named a round or event
logical_time.hour: a (sitting, round), or an event anchor such as event/subcommittee-reported
logical_time.event_scope_tokens: 'just-now' / 'now' = the first round addressed to the state in which the event occurred; 'since-ruling' / 'pending-consent' / 'open-now' = the window from that event's round until the next admitted non-challenge act. These are DEFINITIONS filling gaps.json event-scope-sugar, not translations of existing rules
